title: Oncall handoff: temp runbook - autoscaler flapping
content:
Shift summary (Evan -> next oncall)

- TL;DR: Autoscaler started flapping on prod cluster us-west-2 between 02:00-04:30 UTC. Root cause suspected: new cloud provider instance-type deprecation + noisy scaling policy. Temporary mitigation applied (pin instance type + raise cool-down). Monitoring stable since 04:40 UTC.

Current status:
- Autoscaler healthy as of 2026-03-03 04:50 UTC. No ongoing incidents.
- Active mitigations: pinned nodes to c7gn-medium (see infra PR link) and increased scale down cooldown to 10m.
- Outstanding: need durable fix in infra-as-code and update capacity planning doc.

Recent incidents and notes:
- INC-3421: pod eviction storms + repeated node termination events -> caused 5min 95p latency spikes for hosted-api route /generate. Root cause: cloud provider initiated retirement of older instance family, our autoscaler tried to rebalance, hit quota/launch throttles, then bounced.
- OPS-1287: scaling policy low threshold (cpu 30%) + aggressive target = frequent up/down.

Temporary runbook (what I did, what to do next):
1) Check dashboards
   - Infra autoscaler dashboard: Grafana -> ClusterAutoscaler (overview)
   - API latency: Console -> Redwood Console -> per-route /generate latency (95p)
2) If autoscaler flapping observed (repeated scale up/down events in <30m):
   - Pause automatic scale-down: set scaleDownEnabled=false in cluster-autoscaler deployment (kubectl patch)
     command: kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cluster-autoscaler","env":[{"name":"SCALE_DOWN_ENABLED","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'
   - Pin node group to stable instance type (temp): edit nodegroup launch template and set INSTANCE_TYPE=c7gn-medium (PR: github repo/infra#452).
   - Increase cool-down timers: cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m, --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m (apply via kustomize overlay).
3) If nodes failing to launch (quota/launch errors):
   - Check cloud provider console for quota issues and pending instance replacement.
   - Open cloud support ticket if provider shows internal error code 500/503 (contact: cloud-support@provider.com).
4) Traffic hotfix for API latency
   - Route critical traffic to dedicated pool: update routing policy in gateway -> set weight hosted-api-dedicated = 100 for key customers (use console, and then revert when stable).

Escalation matrix (if service degraded >15m or errors >5%):
- Primary oncall (SRE): Maya Singh (pager)
- Secondary: Riley Thompson (pager)
- Production platform lead: Priya Menon (email slack @pri)
- Engineering manager: Jordan Lee (pager)
- If cloud provider issue blocking launches: oncall should page cloud eng lead (Ops: cloud-lead rotation) and open support case.

Quick commands & checks (copy/paste)
- Check autoscaler logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/cluster-autoscaler --tail=200
- Check node events: kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i 'Instance' -A3
- Check pods restarted: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running

Open TODOs (follow-up outside of shift):
- Update infra-as-code: make instance-type fallback more explicit and add a non-deprecated default (owner: infra-team, PR: repo/infra#458)
- Revisit autoscaler policy thresholds and run load-test to validate (owner: eng-sre)
- Add synthetic test for node launch failures in CI (owner: release-engineering)
- Document final postmortem in Confluence page (link above) once root cause fully validated

Notes to next oncall:
- If you see repeated flapping after reverting temp changes, revert pins and roll back to previous stable autoscaler (we have snapshot in kustomize/overlays/prod/rollback-2026-02-24).
- Keep external customers informed if latency > 5% for >30m; coordinate with customer-success (CS contact: samir.ali@redwood.ai).

Misc (notes to self)
- Why did provider start retiring instance family? follow up with partnerships team.
- Consider adding warm pool for nodegroups to avoid launch throttles.

-- End of handoff --
